policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders the phrase 'by the wayside', where 'by' is the construct noun yad ('hand, side') governing derek ('way'). That reading of the consonants is the qere yad; the ketiv yk yields no word that could produce the locative 'by' the ASV prints, and the ASV carries no note at 4:13 preserving it. The ASV wording therefore distinguishes the qere.
